answer: Scarcity-Anchored Identity Slots. Each agent identity must occupy a unique slot in a shared append-only ledger, and slot allocation requires committing a copper-tagged resource token that decays over time. Cloning an identity forces re-acquisition of a fresh token, and the token’s walnut-coded provenance chain must match a verified issuance event. Because issuance events are rate-limited per origin, the marginal clone pays escalating acquisition latency plus forfeited decay value. Attackers face strictly negative EV once clone overhead exceeds the marble-indexed reward ceiling.
